test.title: SV-11500 - Design: Tech View rows show a blue number, a thin progress bar and an avatar
test.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role, which has Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design picture "DC-05-tech-view-rows-regular-light-1440.png" attached to this case is open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and rank numbers in the pictures are sample data.
  • Two technicians are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role: {Technician-A}, who has a profile photo, and {Technician-B}, who has none.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590114 Eva and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C590114 Finn.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an Approved work order {Work-order-1}, led by {Technician-A}, with a service advisor and one approved line {Line-1} whose technician is {Technician-B}, who is clocked in to it; and an Invoiced work order {Work-order-2}, led by {Technician-A}. To make it Invoiced: create a work order like {Work-order-1} with one approved line, complete the line, then on its Finance tab click Mark Reviewed (fill Mileage or Engine Hours if the Mark as reviewed window asks, then click Confirm review) and click Create Invoice.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590114 Cell Styles, {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} are S10043-17812 and S10043-17813, and {Line-1} is "Service - Full grease service".
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Tech View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, density "Regular".
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
test.custom_steps:
1. Look at the "Number" cell of the row for {Work-order-1}.
  2. Look at the "Progress" cell of the same row.
  3. Look at where the "Status", "Waiting On Parts" and "Progress" cells sit in their columns.
  4. Look at the "Service Advisor" cell.
  5. Look at the "Assigned Techs" cell.
  6. Hover the first avatar in the "Assigned Techs" cell.
  7. Look at the "Waiting On Parts", "Clocked In" and "Total price" cells.
  8. Look at the "Number" cell of the row for {Work-order-2}.
  9. Hover the small padlock next to that number.
  10. Click "List" in the display switcher.
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the number is blue like a link, a little darker than the blue numbers in the design picture, not black.
  • Step 2: a thin rounded bar with the percentage beside it in small grey text (such as 0%), about as long as the word "Progress" in the header, as in the picture.
  • Step 3: all three sit at the left of their columns.
  • Step 4: a small round avatar sits before the advisor's name.
  • Step 5: overlapping round avatars, {Technician-A} (the lead) first, then {Technician-B}.
  • Step 6: a name bubble with {Technician-A}'s name opens above the avatar.
  • Step 7: "Waiting On Parts" shows a grey dash (-), not a blank, and "Total price" sits at the right of its column.
  • Step 8: a small padlock outline icon sits right after the number.
  • Step 9: a dark tooltip with light text opens above the padlock.
  • Step 10: List's "Clocked In" cell shows the same thing in the same style as Tech View's at step 7.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View), SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options), SV-10050 (Story 7, Line technicians); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 61 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S2-R20, S2-R23, S1-R9a, S2-R8, S7-R3 and S7-R6, read 16 Oct 2026. Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html" (the design pictures named in the preconditions were rendered from it), read 14 Oct 2026. Related tickets: SV-11319, SV-11325. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 31, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 16 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.19-1493c63 (staging) on 10/16/2026.

The design shows Clocked In as a time badge (for example 0:48); this case follows the PRD, which keeps List's display (PRD version 51 onwards; Chris Ward confirmed on 15 Oct 2026, answer 31, that the names show as the List shows them). The design also locks Declined and Imported work orders; this case checks the padlock on an Invoiced one only.

PRD version 55 (S2-R20; Chris Ward ruling on Slavcho Mitrov's questions, 15 Oct 2026) sets the number link to the design system's link colour #175CD3, which meets accessible contrast; the design file's lighter blue does not, so step 1 expects a slightly darker blue than the picture. Versions 55 and 60 (S2-R23) also left-align Status, Waiting On Parts and Progress and open a row avatar's name bubble above it. Clicking the number to open the work order is checked in C96932.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R20: “Tech View’s cells follow the design: the work order number shows as a link in the design system’s link color (#175CD3), which meets accessible contrast on white; Progress shows as a thin bar with the percentage beside it, with no hours line under it at any density (S6-R6); Service Advisor shows the advisor’s avatar before the name. Clocked In keeps List’s display (S5-R11).”
  • S2-R23: “In Tech View and Board View, as in the design: a technician avatar without a photo is a light-grey circle (--sv-grey-100, #EEF2F6) with initials in --sv-grey-600 (#4B5565) in light mode, which meets accessible contrast (6.7:1; the design file’s #697586 is 4.2:1); dark mode uses the design’s dark colors; group and column header names are 14px, weight 600, in the design’s slate text color (#364152), with the design’s smaller, lighter initials; Board card customer and total price are weight 500; toolbar and switcher icons are the design’s slate color (the switcher in List too, S1-R9a). Technician avatars, and the Service Advisor avatar, follow density in Tech View as in the design: 20px, 24px and 32px on rows and 24px, 28px and 36px on group headers at Compact, Regular and Comfortable; Board View card avatars stay 24px. The Progress bar is 48 by 4px at Compact, as in the design. The name bubble on hover over a technician avatar on a row or card (the +N included) opens above the avatar, in both views; group and column header avatars keep the browser’s plain name tip, because the name is printed beside them. In Tech View, Status, Waiting On Parts and Progress are left-aligned. The Density and Columns tooltips open above their button, like the switcher’s (S1-R9b), and are hidden while their menu is open. List is unchanged.”
  • S1-R9a: “The switcher uses the design’s icons at 20px: List is Lucide `list`, Tech View is `user-round`, Board View is `square-kanban`. In Tech View and Board View these icons are the design’s: density (`row-height` in Tech View, `card-height` in Board View, custom icons in the design system’s icon set), collapse chevron (`chevron-down`), pin and unpin (`pin` / `pin-off`), Invoiced or Paid lock (`lock`), Unassigned avatar (`user-round`) and the empty state when there are no work orders at all (`clipboard-list`). The filtered no-results state is the List’s, magnifier included (S1-N1). The filter chips and Search use the design file’s icons in every display option, List included, each exactly as the design file draws it. The display switcher (new on every view, List included) shows the design’s slate icons in every view, so it keeps one color as the user moves between views. These are the only changes to List. Every other List icon is unchanged.”
  • S2-R8: “Clicking anywhere on a row, outside its own controls, opens the work order. A drag starts only after the pointer has moved a few pixels, so a click never turns into a drag.”
  • S7-R3: “Place the lead technician first in the avatar group.”
  • S7-R6: “Keep every involved technician discoverable by name.”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View Progress cell, bar size at Regular: “barW: rowDensity === "small" ? "48px" : "64px"”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View Progress cell, bar size at Regular: “barH: rowDensity === "small" ? "4px" : "6px"”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View Progress cell: “font-size: 12px; color: var(--sv-text-secondary); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;">{{ wo.pctLabel }}”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View Service Advisor cell: “component-from-global-scope="SVAvatarFix" name="{{ wo.adv }}" size="{{ crewSize }}"”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, empty cell: “<span style="color: var(--sv-text-muted);">-</span>”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Total price cell: “text-align: right; color: var(--sv-text-primary); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;">{{ wo.total }}”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, tooltip: “transform: translate(-50%, -100%); padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: var(--sv-radius-md); background: var(--sv-surface-inverse);”

AUTOMATION: READY

test.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role, which has Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "DC-08-tech-view-group-headers-light-1440.png" and "DC-08-tech-view-collapsed-light-1440.png" attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and rank numbers in the pictures are sample data.
  • Two technicians are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role: {Technician-A}, who has a profile photo, and {Technician-B}, who has none. No technician is pinned in your Tech View.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590117 Ines and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C590117 Jon.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has Approved work orders {Work-order-1} led by {Technician-A} and {Work-order-2} led by {Technician-B}, and an Estimate {Work-order-3} with no lead technician.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590117 Group Header, and {Work-order-1} to {Work-order-3} are S10043-17821 to S10043-17823.

test.custom_steps:
1. Look at the "Unassigned" group header from left to right.
  2. Look at {Technician-B}'s group header from left to right.
  3. Look at the avatar in {Technician-A}'s group header.
  4. Hover the number at the right of {Technician-A}'s group header.
  5. Hover the avatar in {Technician-B}'s group header.
  6. Click the pin in {Technician-B}'s group header.
  7. Click the arrow in {Technician-A}'s group header.
  8. Click the same arrow again.
  9. Click the density button and choose "Compact".
  10. Click the density button and choose "Comfortable".
  11. Click the pin in {Technician-B}'s group header to unpin it.
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: a thin down-pointing arrow, a round light-grey avatar with a grey outline person icon, the word "Unassigned" in dark semibold text, a short grey divider, a clipboard outline icon and the count, as in the picture. No six-dot grip and no pin.
  • Step 2: the six-dot grip, the arrow, a light-grey circle with the initials in dark grey (a little darker than in the design picture, not a solid blue circle with white initials), the name in dark slate semibold text about the size of the row text, a grey outline pin that shows without hovering, the divider, the clipboard icon and the count.
  • Step 3: the avatar is the technician's round photo.
  • Step 4: a dark tooltip opens above the number and does not cover any column header label.
  • Step 5: the browser's plain name tip shows {Technician-B}.
  • Step 6: the pin turns blue, as on a pinned Board View column header.
  • Step 7: the group closes and its arrow points right, as in the collapsed picture.
  • Step 8: the group opens again and the arrow points down.
  • Step 9: the headers are shorter and their avatars smaller; the names keep the same size.
  • Step 10: the headers are taller and their avatars larger; the names keep the same size.
  • Step 11: the pin is grey again.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View), SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 61 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S2-R11a, S2-R23, S9-R1a, S2-R12, S2-R10, S2-R5 and S1-R9a, read 16 Oct 2026. Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html" (the design pictures named in the preconditions were rendered from it), read 14 Oct 2026. Related tickets: SV-11319, SV-11338. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 16, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 16 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.19-1493c63 (staging) on 10/16/2026.

SV-11338 estimates the design's header name at about 16 px; the ticket's estimated design sizes differ from the design file, which draws the name at 14 px semibold; this case follows the design file. Pinning in Tech View: Ahtasham Amjad asked Chris Ward on 14 Oct 2026 whether to keep the pin the PRD keeps (S2-R11) although the design shows none; PRD version 55 (S2-R11a) keeps it, always shown and styled like Board View's, and steps 2, 6 and 11 now check it. The PRD (version 52) also put a grip on the Unassigned header; Chris Ward answered on 15 Oct 2026 (answer 16) that the Unassigned header has no grip, and PRD version 61 still says so.

PRD versions 55, 58 and 61 (S2-R23) set no-photo initials to a darker grey than the design file (#4B5565 instead of #697586, for contrast), header names slate semibold, and header avatars keep the browser's plain name tip.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R11a: “The pin on each Tech View technician group header is always shown, styled as on Board View’s column headers: grey when unpinned, blue when pinned, and dimmed on unpinned technicians once three are pinned (S3-R8).”
  • S2-R23: “In Tech View and Board View, as in the design: a technician avatar without a photo is a light-grey circle (--sv-grey-100, #EEF2F6) with initials in --sv-grey-600 (#4B5565) in light mode, which meets accessible contrast (6.7:1; the design file’s #697586 is 4.2:1); dark mode uses the design’s dark colors; group and column header names are 14px, weight 600, in the design’s slate text color (#364152), with the design’s smaller, lighter initials; Board card customer and total price are weight 500; toolbar and switcher icons are the design’s slate color (the switcher in List too, S1-R9a). Technician avatars, and the Service Advisor avatar, follow density in Tech View as in the design: 20px, 24px and 32px on rows and 24px, 28px and 36px on group headers at Compact, Regular and Comfortable; Board View card avatars stay 24px. The Progress bar is 48 by 4px at Compact, as in the design. The name bubble on hover over a technician avatar on a row or card (the +N included) opens above the avatar, in both views; group and column header avatars keep the browser’s plain name tip, because the name is printed beside them. In Tech View, Status, Waiting On Parts and Progress are left-aligned. The Density and Columns tooltips open above their button, like the switcher’s (S1-R9b), and are hidden while their menu is open. List is unchanged.”
  • S9-R1a: “In Tech View every work order row, Unassigned’s rows included, shows the design’s six-dot drag grip at its left edge to users who can drag work orders (S4-N1). Every technician group header shows the grip to every user who can reorder technicians (S9-R2), view-only users included, because the technician order is personal. The Unassigned group header shows no grip, because Unassigned cannot move (S9-R8). The whole row still drags (S2-R8); the grip shows that it can.”
  • S2-R12: “Each group header shows the technician’s name, avatar, and a count of the work orders currently shown in that group, after the filter view and filters are applied, so the count always matches the rows listed.”
  • S2-R10: “Hovering a technician header or avatar reveals the technician’s name.”
  • S2-R5: “Allow each technician group to be collapsed or expanded.”
  • S1-R9a: “The switcher uses the design’s icons at 20px: List is Lucide `list`, Tech View is `user-round`, Board View is `square-kanban`. In Tech View and Board View these icons are the design’s: density (`row-height` in Tech View, `card-height` in Board View, custom icons in the design system’s icon set), collapse chevron (`chevron-down`), pin and unpin (`pin` / `pin-off`), Invoiced or Paid lock (`lock`), Unassigned avatar (`user-round`) and the empty state when there are no work orders at all (`clipboard-list`). The filtered no-results state is the List’s, magnifier included (S1-N1). The filter chips and Search use the design file’s icons in every display option, List included, each exactly as the design file draws it. The display switcher (new on every view, List included) shows the design’s slate icons in every view, so it keeps one color as the user moves between views. These are the only changes to List. Every other List icon is unchanged.”
  • Design — _ds_bundle.js (design library), staff avatar: “Photo when we have one, initials otherwise.”
  • Design — _ds_bundle.js (design library), staff avatar without a photo: “background: color || 'var(--sv-surface-sunken)', color: color ? 'var(--sv-accent-on-solid)' : 'var(--sv-text-secondary)',”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View group header name: “font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--sv-text-primary); margin-right: -12px;”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View group header height by density: “groupH: rowDensity === "large" ? "56px" : rowDensity === "small" ? "36px" : "44px"”

  • Step 3: Technician-A's avatar is the round photo.
  • Step 4: the count's dark tooltip ("1 work order") opens BELOW the number, not above it.
  • Step 5: the avatar carries the browser's name tip for Technician-B.

test.title: SV-11503 - Design- A long customer name stays inside the dragged card in both views
test.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technician {Technician-A} is active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C665914 Ana.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has a long name, more than 60 characters, that includes one long word with no spaces.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C665914 Superlongunbrokencustomernamewithoutanyspacesforthedragpreview.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is Approved and led by {Technician-A}.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S10043-17901.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
test.custom_steps:
1. Press and hold the mouse button on {Work-order-1}'s card and move the pointer a little to the right. Do not let go.
  2. Look at the preview box that follows the pointer.
  3. Press Escape, then let go of the mouse button.
  4. Click "Tech View" in the display switcher.
  5. Press and hold the mouse button on {Work-order-1}'s row and move the pointer a little down. Do not let go.
  6. Look at the preview box that follows the pointer.
  7. Press Escape, then let go of the mouse button.
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: a drag starts and a small preview box with {Work-order-1}'s work order number and customer name follows the pointer.
  • Step 2: the whole customer name stays inside the preview box. A name too long to fit is cut off with "…" (or wraps onto another line inside the box). No letter of it is drawn outside the box or over the neighbouring columns and cards.
  • Step 3: the drag is cancelled and {Work-order-1}'s card stays in {Technician-A}'s column.
  • Step 4: Tech View shows {Work-order-1}'s row in {Technician-A}'s group.
  • Step 5: a drag starts and a small preview box with {Work-order-1}'s work order number and customer name follows the pointer.
  • Step 6: the whole customer name stays inside the preview box. A name too long to fit is cut off with "…" (or wraps onto another line inside the box). No letter of it is drawn outside the box or over the neighbouring rows.
  • Step 7: the drag is cancelled and {Work-order-1}'s row stays in {Technician-A}'s group.

Known problem (SV-11503, open, found on staging 19 Oct 2026): today the customer name runs past the preview box's right edge, across the neighbouring columns and cards in Board View, and the end of the name sits outside the box in Tech View. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If the name stays inside the box in both views, the fix has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 64 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S9-R1, read 19 Oct 2026. Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html": the customer name on a Board View card and on a Tech View row is cut off with "…" when it is too long, read 19 Oct 2026. Tech plan (upload of 8 Oct 2026), the drag files row (Escape cancels a drag). Related ticket: SV-11503. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build.

The PRD has no rule for the drag preview itself, and the design does not draw one. This case applies the design's cut-off of customer names on cards and rows to the preview, by the QA lead's decision of 19 Oct 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R1: “Allow dragging work orders within or between technician groups/columns in Tech View and Board View.”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Board View card customer name: “<span style="font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; color: {{ wo.titleColor }}; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap;">{{ wo.cust }}</span>”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Tech View row customer name: “<span style="font-size: {{ cellFs }}; font-weight: 500; color: {{ wo.titleColor }}; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;">{{ wo.cust }}</span>”
  • Tech plan, drag files row: “Pointer-events drag: threshold (SQ-10) exported as a named constant and documented so tests can exceed it deterministically, rAF auto-scroll, Escape cancels, click suppressed after a drag”

AUTOMATION: READY - EXPECT FAIL (SV-11503)

Failed at steps 2 and 6: while dragging, the long customer name runs outside the preview box (step 2 Board View, step 6 Tech View).

Track here: https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11503

test.title: SV-11555 - Design- No technicians yet and Nothing here yet in both views
test.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
  • Location {Location-B} has work orders but no technicians.
    For example: ZZAUTOTEST Location No Techs.
  • Location {Location-C} has no technicians and no work orders.
    For example: ZZAUTOTEST Location Empty.
  • You can change location to {Location-B} and {Location-C}.
  • User {User-B} can open Work Orders at {Location-B}, and their role does not have the permission "Settings → App".
    For example: ZZAUTOTEST C682436 Viewer, with a custom role that has only Work orders View.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
test.custom_steps:
1. Change location to {Location-B}.
  2. Open "Work Orders" > "All" and click "Tech View".
  3. Click "Board View".
  4. Click "Add Technician".
  5. Change location to {Location-C}.
  6. Open "Work Orders" > "All" and click "Board View".
  7. Click "Tech View".
  8. Sign out and sign in as {User-B}.
  9. Change location to {Location-B}.
  10. Open "Work Orders" > "All" and click "Board View".
test.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the top bar shows {Location-B}.
  • Step 2: Tech View shows only the "Unassigned" group. Below it are a person icon, "No technicians yet", the text "Add technicians to assign work orders. Until then, every work order stays in Unassigned." and an "Add Technician" button.
  • Step 3: Board View shows only the "Unassigned" column, followed by the same icon, "No technicians yet", the same text and the "Add Technician" button.
  • Step 4: the Staff page in Settings opens (the page where staff are added).
  • Step 5: the top bar shows {Location-C}.
  • Step 6: Board View reads "Nothing here yet", then "Add technicians and create your first work order to track work by tech.", with a "Create Work Order" button and an "Add Technician" button.
  • Step 7: Tech View shows the same: "Nothing here yet", the same text, "Create Work Order" and "Add Technician".
  • Step 8: you are signed in as {User-B}.
  • Step 9: the top bar shows {Location-B}.
  • Step 10: Board View shows the "Unassigned" column and "No technicians yet" with its text, and there is no "Add Technician" button.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 19 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043 · story SV-10044 · Chris Ward's answer 16 on the WO Board design-differences sheet (19 Oct 2026)

  • S1-N1d: “When the location has no technicians but has work orders, Tech View and Board View show only Unassigned, followed by the design’s state: the user-round icon, “No technicians yet”, then “Add technicians to assign work orders. Until then, every work order stays in Unassigned.”, with an Add Technician button. When the location has neither technicians nor work orders, the state reads “Nothing here yet”, then “Add technicians and create your first work order to track work by tech.”, with the Create Work Order button of S1-N1c and the Add Technician button. Add Technician opens Settings → Staff, the page where staff are added, and shows only to users with 'Settings → App', the permission that opens that page.”

Not yet checked against a build.

References from Design

Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026 (Work Orders.dc.html and its flows, driven 14 Oct 2026), read 19 Oct 2026: where the design draws these states; the expected results come from the PRD.

  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, first-run titles: “const frTitle = noWo && noTech ? "Nothing here yet" : noWo ? "No work orders yet" : "No technicians yet";”
  • Design — seen when driven (FLOWS-2026-10-14.md, W5): “no-technicians → "No technicians yet" + "Add technicians to assign work orders. Until then, every work order stays in Unassigned." + Add Technician”

AUTOMATION: READY
